purpose: Separate logical worker count from physical executor count and let measured workload physics govern concurrency.

workerModel.logicalWorkers: Agent-level task lanes; may exceed physical CPU/GPU executors.
workerModel.law: Never equate 20 logical workers with 20 OS threads.

observationWindow.rule: 16 comparable workload windows under one scheduler, workload class and executor topology.

cpuBound.finding: 20 OS threads are substantially worse than one for this small CPU-bound kernel.

waitHeavy.workload: synthetic training-orchestration proxy; 200 tasks; 20ms wait plus deterministic hash work
waitHeavy.finding: 20 logical async workers substantially outperform one when latency can be overlapped.

target: Make 20 logical Agent Lee workers outperform one on real training orchestration while allowing Formula to choose the smaller physical executor pool.
claimBoundary: The 20-worker win is proven only on the synthetic wait-heavy orchestration proxy; QLoRA/DPO training has not yet been benchmarked.
